decision_description: The revision integrator dispositioned the ten revision actions in the Phase 8 review packet. One action, A-5, is resolved by existing prose: the Impact section already states which part of the fourth destination impact the evidence base satisfies, namely that the project improves the evidence a biodiversity valuation rests on and runs no valuation because no partner carries environmental economics. The remaining nine actions are deferred as unresolved and carried to an operator-directed revision cycle. Each requires a project fact or a consortium commitment that no confirmed Tier 3 source carries: per-work-package and per-partner person-months (A-1), confirmed beneficiaries and a second freshwater and marine partner (A-2), KPI target numbers (A-3), cited prior results and a quantified comparison (A-4), impact-indicator targets (A-6), confirmed uptake, protocol-transfer and standards partners (A-7), work-package and milestone months (A-8), gender-of-research expertise in the consortium (A-9), and the analytical method and reporting deliverable for the sex- and gender-disaggregated analysis (A-10). Phase 8f performed no automated prose revision on the nine deferred actions.
alternatives_considered: Close the nine actions by seeding person-months, KPI and impact targets, work-package and milestone months, and confirmed partner participation. Rejected: these are project facts and consortium commitments absent from Tier 3, and inventing them violates CLAUDE.md §13.3.

Mark the implementation, excellence and impact sections final and set data_gaps_flagged true without recording the deferral. Rejected: the gaps are flagged in the section prose and must be surfaced, not silently closed, per CLAUDE.md §13.8.
Compute cost-bearing effort internally to satisfy A-1. Rejected: this is a lump-sum topic, so effort tied to cost is set against the externally validated budget per CLAUDE.md §13.4 and §8.3.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §13.3 (project facts and consortium commitments absent from Tier 3 may not be fabricated); CLAUDE.md §13.4 and §8.3 (cost-bearing effort for a lump-sum topic is set against the externally validated budget, not generated internally); CLAUDE.md §13.8 (known gaps are flagged in the deliverable, not filled with fabricated content)
rationale: Nine of the ten review-packet actions ask for facts the confirmed tiers do not hold. All twelve partners are operator assumptions, and P07 to P12 are fictional gap partners, so participation, effort, targets and gender expertise cannot be asserted as confirmed. The honest disposition is to flag each gap in the section prose and defer its closure to an operator-directed revision cycle once participation and the validated budget are confirmed. A-5 is resolved because the drafted prose already satisfies the recommendation's second branch. Recording this disposition in the decision log keeps the deferred gaps visible to downstream review rather than leaving them only in the phase output, per CLAUDE.md §9.4.
